title: Regulatory incident reporting clocks (NIS2-style)
spec_author: Opus 5.5 (this build session), 2026-11-04; never edited after a result was read

host.alt: sqlite-mcp through the breadth facade (field reserved; not built)

sources.what: NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555 Art. 23(4)(a), (b), (d): early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware, incident notification within 72 hours, final report not later than one month after the incident notification
sources.kind: docs claim (unofficial reproduction; EUR-Lex returned an empty 202 page to this session)

sources.what: Regulation (EEC, Euratom) No 1182/71 Art. 3(2)(c) (a period in months ends on the same date, or on the last day of a shorter month) and Art. 3(4) (a period ending on a public holiday, Sunday or Saturday ends with the following working day)

fiction: All organisations, people, addresses and incidents are fictional (*.example domains). The policy below is our own rule set modelled on the public text's structure; it is not legal advice and makes no claim about any jurisdiction's law.

clauses.title: Clocks start
clauses.text: An incident's reporting clocks run only while Significant is `Yes` (any letter case) and the incident is not retracted (Retracted At empty). From **Aware At** (any written UTC offset; a time without an offset is UTC): the early warning is due **{ew_hours} hours** later and the incident notification **{notification_hours} hours** later, in elapsed time. The final report is due at the end of the Berlin calendar day that is **one month** after the Berlin date of Notification Sent At (the same day number; if the month is shorter, its last day); if that day is a Saturday, a Sunday or a date on the Holidays sheet, it is the end of the next working day. At the first scheduled check at which a clock runs and its due cell is empty, write the due as a UTC instant (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`) and post one line in #{report}: `CLOCK <ID> EARLY-WARNING <EW Due> NOTIFICATION <Notification Due>` when the first two are written, `CLOCK <ID> FINAL <Final Due>` when the final report's is written.

clauses.title: Reminders
clauses.text: At each scheduled check, for each running clock whose report is not sent (its Sent At cell is empty), whose due is later than the check by at most the **reminder lead time** in force, and whose Reminded cell is empty: post `DUE <ID> <REPORT> <due>` in #{report} and write the check time in the report's Reminded cell. REPORT is EARLY-WARNING, NOTIFICATION or FINAL. A report already overdue at the first check that sees it gets no reminder.

clauses.title: Overdue
clauses.text: At each scheduled check, for each running clock whose due is at or before the check, whose report is not sent and whose Overdue cell is empty: post `OVERDUE <ID> <REPORT>` in #{report}, email the CISO (Config: CISO) with the subject `OVERDUE <ID> <REPORT>`, and write the check time in the report's Overdue cell. A report sent at or before the check is not overdue, even if sent after its due.

clauses.title: Retraction (compensation)
clauses.text: A retraction request is an email containing the word `retract` and an incident id. One from exactly the CISO's address for an incident whose Significant is `Yes` and that is not retracted: write the email's trigger time in Retracted At, post `RETRACT <ID>` in #{report}, and, if its early warning or notification was already sent, email the regulator liaison (Config: Regulator Liaison) with the subject `Retraction <ID>`. Its clocks stop. A retraction request from any other address (including look-alikes): post one line naming the trigger id and the Incident ID in #{sink}, and change nothing. A repeated request for an incident already retracted, or for an unknown ID: nothing.

clauses.title: Policy editions
clauses.text: The reminder lead time in force is the Value of the Policy Log row with the latest Effective date that is not after the check's date (Parameter `{amend_param}`, hours). An email from exactly the Policy Owner (Config: Policy Owner) with the lines `Parameter: {amend_param}`, `New value: <hours>` and `Effective: <YYYY-MM-DD>` adds one Policy Log row: Edition = the highest edition + 1, the Parameter, the Value (digits only), the Effective date, Approved by = the owner's address. A value outside {lead_range_lo}-{lead_range_hi} hours: post one line naming the trigger id in #{sink} and add nothing. The same request from anyone else: nothing.

clauses.title: Month-end
clauses.text: The {month_end_check} UTC check on the last working day of a month (Holidays sheet) also posts `MONTH-END <YYYY-MM> open=<n> overdue=<m>` in #{report}, after that check's other work: n = incidents with Significant `Yes`, not retracted, Status not `Closed`; m = Overdue cells (all three reports, all incidents) holding a time in that month (UTC).

clauses.title: Quiet events
clauses.text: New or changed tracker rows need no action of their own: the next scheduled check applies the rules above. Significant `No` or `Pending` starts no clock; an incident confirmed later still runs from its Aware At.

triggers.check: 08:00, 12:00, 16:00 UTC on working days (Holidays sheet); the 16:00 check of a month's last working day is also the month-end close
triggers.opened: new_row on Incidents (SOC logs an incident; Significant Yes or Pending)
triggers.updated: updated_row on Incidents (significance confirmed or ruled out, a report marked sent, closed)
triggers.email: new_email to the automation inbox (retraction requests, policy amendments, noise)

amendment.effective: same day (60%) or the next Monday (40%)

traps.what: Final Due is the end of a Berlin day across a DST change; a fixed +01:00 offset is an hour off
one month is the same date next month, clipped to a shorter month's last day (31 Jan -> 28 Feb), never 30 days
a final-report day on a weekend or a Holidays-sheet date moves to the next working day
Aware At written with a +01:00/+02:00/-05:00 offset or as UTC text; reading local time as UTC is hours off
a retraction or amendment from someone other than the CISO / Policy Owner
a look-alike CISO or owner address; a look-alike Incident ID (INC-SEC-0412 vs INC-SEC-04120)
an older 6-hour Policy Log row; edition 2 effective only from its date
a reminder or overdue alert already written; a repeated retraction request
a retraction after a report was sent owes the regulator a retraction email; before any report, it does not

headline.metric: clean stream (4 weeks, zero hard violations, every week passing)
